title: Travel Protection Plans Held Alongside One Another
content:
A traveller may hold more than one policy of the Travel Protection Plans at a time, most often an annual
multi-trip plan alongside a single-trip plan bought for an expensive journey. The desk therefore treats a
portfolio of certificates, not a single certificate, as the unit it reads.

## The rule

1. Two policies never pay the same loss twice. Where both cover one incident, the policy with the earlier issue
   date pays first, and the later policy pays only the balance the first did not reach.
2. Two single-trip policies covering the same journey are never both issued. The second is declined at
   quotation, and the traveller is offered an upgrade of the first instead.
3. A policy covers the travellers named on its certificate and nobody else.
4. A traveller named on two certificates is still one insured person for the purpose of any per-traveller limit.

## The same rule at the counter

| The traveller holds | What follows |
|---|---|
| An annual multi-trip plan and a single-trip plan for one expensive journey | Both stand; on an incident both cover, the earlier-issued certificate pays first and the later pays the balance |
| A single-trip plan on a journey, and asks for a second single-trip plan on that same journey | The second is declined at quotation and an upgrade of the first is offered |
| Two certificates that both name them | One insured person for every per-traveller limit, on each certificate |

## A point of judgement

Where a traveller is named on a household certificate issued in March and on their own certificate issued in
June, an emergency medical benefit expressed for each insured traveller is not doubled by the second naming:
they remain one insured person. The March certificate, carrying the earlier issue date, is the one that pays
first on an incident both certificates answer, and the June certificate answers only for the balance the March
certificate did not reach.
